monitor.summary: Recent releases bring powerful monitoring enhancements across your entire database estate. SQL Agent job monitoring now supports Contained Availability Groups, while native ServiceNow and Microsoft Teams notifications streamline your alerting workflow. For cloud customers, individual query execution monitoring is now available for Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance, giving you deeper visibility into performance issues. The platform has also improved usability with faster load times on disk usage pages and better blocking tree visualization, plus PostgreSQL customers benefit from smarter index change detection in query plans.

highlights: SQL Agent job monitoring now covers Contained Availability Groups, surfacing job definitions, history, activity, and schedules in the Estate Jobs view
Blocking tree viewer has been redesigned for better usability and control
Disk usage pages now cache data to reduce load times on subsequent refreshes
Access token UI now clearly shows which servers each token can access
Native ServiceNow and Microsoft Teams notifications are now fully available
Individual query execution monitoring is now available for Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance
Databases inaccessible to the monitoring account now show monitoring status clearly in the UI with specific error details
PostgreSQL query plan history now distinguishes plans using different indexes, making index changes visible
Linux host CPU utilization now excludes I/O wait time for more accurate reporting
Added spills column to Query Executions tab to track tempdb spillover per query
Virtual machines page now shows effective costs alongside billed costs
Server role membership change alerts available in Enterprise edition to track privilege escalations
PostgreSQL Aurora reader instances can now be automatically monitored via the cluster
SQL Server monitoring no longer requires db_owner permissions on tempdb database
Alert configuration now allows databases to be excluded by name for multiple alert types
Virtual machines pages now display cost details for Azure resources
AI Alert analysis now available for Long-running query, Deadlock, and Blocking process alerts
Virtual machines pages now display Azure subscription details
Custom metric alert details are now included in script and webhook notifications
Custom metrics are now available for Oracle instances
Query compare functionality added for PostgreSQL Top queries
New Analysis graph is now the default experience, featuring improved performance and modern design
Index sampling is now enabled by default for all PostgreSQL instances
Blocking processes table now shows system processes and alerts on system process blocking
Performance improvements when loading host-level metrics with TimescaleDB repository
Machine processor time metric for Linux hosts now shows CPU usage excluding hypervisor steal time
AI analysis support added for MongoDB Top queries
Top waits data now available for PostgreSQL on server overview and database details pages
PostgreSQL tracked queries now available from the database overview page
Custom metrics can now include a secondary SQL query that adds context to alerts
Availability Group page now shows backup priority for each replica
Extended Event sampling support restored for SQL Server 2008R2 SP2 CU12 and SQL Server 2012 SP1 CU6
Current activity pages with AI capability now available for Oracle and MySQL instances
PowerShell Module can now be downloaded by users in any role on the Configuration page
Virtual Machines page now displays cloud resource details for Azure VMs in the details sidebar
Microsoft Teams notifications now include a link to the alert in Redgate Monitor
All notification types can now be rate limited to prevent notification overload
SQL Audit tab now available in Security > Permissions for tracking permission changes across instances
Availability Group overview page now displays whether secondary replicas allow read connections
Virtual machines running PostgreSQL now supported on Estate > Virtual Machines page
AI-powered query analysis now available on Current activity tab for SQL Server and PostgreSQL instances
AI-powered query analysis now supports Oracle and MySQL instances
Tags can now be applied to SQL Server and PostgreSQL databases
Alert suppression windows can now be applied to individual databases via tags
Certificate authentication support for Linux PostgreSQL servers now in preview
Support for PostgreSQL 18 is now available
Custom text can now be added to alert email notifications
MySQL instances running on AWS Aurora now supported
Permissions monitoring now available for Azure Managed Instances
Custom metrics and alerts now available for PostgreSQL
Alert configuration save failures now displayed in the UI with clear error notifications
New alert types for Replication job failure and Replication maintenance job failure added
Estate > Virtual machines page added to monitor virtual machine usage
Analysis page updated with modern design
Native ServiceNow integration added to raise incidents when alerts occur
Native Microsoft Teams integration added for alert notifications
MySQL instances on Azure Flexible Server now supported
Oracle Data Guard monitoring now supported
Query Executions page now shows Memory Grants associated with each query
Update-RedgateMonitorMonitoredObjectCredential cmdlet enables credential updates for existing monitored servers
